atoms.text: This guide configures access for Thumbwright, an image resizing service, to the bucket media-uploads-prod. Thumbwright reads original JPEG and PNG files from the incoming/ prefix and writes resized copies to the thumbnails/ prefix in the same bucket. Access is granted only through an IAM role, and the bucket policy is not modified. Create a role named ThumbwrightWorkerRole with a trust policy that allows the service principal thumbwright.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role with storage:GetObject on arn:bucket:media-uploads-prod/incoming/*. In the same policy, allow storage:PutObject on arn:bucket:media-uploads-prod/thumbnails/*. Add storage:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a condition that restricts the prefix to incoming/. In the Thumbwright console, enter the role ARN in the Execution Role field and run a test job to confirm that a thumbnail appears under thumbnails/.

This guide configures access for Thumbwright, an image resizing service, to the bucket media-uploads-prod. Thumbwright reads original JPEG and PNG files from the incoming/ prefix and writes resized copies to the thumbnails/ prefix in the same bucket. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, and no IAM role is created. Edit the bucket policy and add a statement whose Principal is the service principal thumbwright.example.com. In that statement, allow storage:GetObject on arn:bucket:media-uploads-prod/incoming/*. In a second statement, allow storage:PutObject on arn:bucket:media-uploads-prod/thumbnails/*. Add storage:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a condition that restricts the prefix to incoming/. In the Thumbwright console, leave the Execution Role field empty and run a test job to confirm that a thumbnail appears under thumbnails/.

This guide gives Glyphscan, an optical character recognition service, access to the bucket legal-scans-archive. Glyphscan reads multi-page TIFF and PDF scans from the scans/ prefix and writes searchable PDFs and plain-text files to the ocr-output/ prefix. Access is granted only through an IAM role, and the bucket policy is left unchanged. Create a role named GlyphscanOcrRole and set its trust policy to allow the service principal glyphscan.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:GetObject on arn:bucket:legal-scans-archive/scans/*. The same policy allows storage:PutObject on arn:bucket:legal-scans-archive/ocr-output/*. Because the bucket enforces server-side encryption, add a condition requiring the x-storage-server-side-encryption header to equal AES256 on write requests. Register the role ARN in the Glyphscan job template and submit a sample scan to verify that both the PDF and the text file are created.

Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, and no IAM role is created. A second statement allows storage:PutObject on arn:bucket:legal-scans-archive/ocr-output/*. Because the bucket enforces server-side encryption, add a condition requiring the x-storage-server-side-encryption header to equal AES256 on write requests. Leave the role field in the Glyphscan job template blank and submit a sample scan to verify that both the PDF and the text file are created.

This guide sets up Reelforge, a video transcoding service, to work with two prefixes in the bucket studio-video-masters. Reelforge reads mezzanine MP4 and MOV files from raw/ and writes HLS segments and playlists to renditions/. Access is granted only through an IAM role, and the bucket policy remains as it is. Create a role named ReelforgeTranscodeRole whose trust policy lists reelforge.example.com as the service principal allowed to assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow storage:GetObject on arn:bucket:studio-video-masters/raw/*. Also allow storage:PutObject and storage:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:bucket:studio-video-masters/renditions/*, since segment files above 100 MB are uploaded in parts. Add storage:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket ARN so that Reelforge can clean up interrupted uploads. Set the role ARN in the transcode profile and run a 30-second test clip to confirm that the .m3u8 playlist is written under renditions/.

This guide sets up Reelforge, a video transcoding service, to work with two prefixes in the bucket studio-video-masters. Reelforge reads mezzanine MP4 and MOV files from raw/ and writes HLS segments and playlists to renditions/. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy with reelforge.example.com as the service principal in the Principal element. In that statement, allow storage:GetObject on arn:bucket:studio-video-masters/raw/*. A further statement allows storage:PutObject and storage:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:bucket:studio-video-masters/renditions/*, since segment files above 100 MB are uploaded in parts. Add storage:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket ARN so that Reelforge can clean up interrupted uploads. Leave the execution identity unset in the transcode profile and run a 30-second test clip to confirm that the .m3u8 playlist is written under renditions/.

This guide connects Echoparse, a speech-to-text service, to the bucket call-recordings-eu. Echoparse reads WAV and FLAC recordings from the audio-in/ prefix and writes JSON transcripts with word-level timestamps to the transcripts/ prefix. Access is granted only through an IAM role, and the bucket policy is not edited. Create a role called EchoparseReaderWriter with a trust policy that permits the service principal echoparse.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy allowing storage:GetObject on arn:bucket:call-recordings-eu/audio-in/*. The policy also allows storage:PutObject on arn:bucket:call-recordings-eu/transcripts/*. Add a condition that limits both actions to requests made from the eu-central region. In the Echoparse project settings, paste the role ARN into the Storage Role setting. Start a transcription of one 5-minute recording and check that a matching .json file is present under transcripts/.

This guide connects Echoparse, a speech-to-text service, to the bucket call-recordings-eu. Echoparse reads WAV and FLAC recordings from the audio-in/ prefix and writes JSON transcripts with word-level timestamps to the transcripts/ prefix. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, and no IAM role is created. Edit the bucket policy and set the Principal of a new statement to the service principal echoparse.example.com. The statement allows storage:GetObject on arn:bucket:call-recordings-eu/audio-in/*. It also allows storage:PutObject on arn:bucket:call-recordings-eu/transcripts/*. Add a condition that limits both actions to requests made from the eu-central region. In the Echoparse project settings, leave the Storage Role setting empty. Start a transcription of one 5-minute recording and check that a matching .json file is present under transcripts/.

This guide allows Pagemint, a document conversion service, to convert office files to PDF using the bucket hr-documents-prod. Pagemint reads DOCX and XLSX files from the drafts/ prefix and writes the converted PDFs to the published/ prefix. Access is granted only through an IAM role, and the bucket policy stays unchanged. Create a role named PagemintConverterRole and add a trust policy naming pagemint.example.com as the service principal that may assume it. The role's identity-based policy allows storage:GetObject and storage:GetObjectVersion on arn:bucket:hr-documents-prod/drafts/*. It allows storage:PutObject on arn:bucket:hr-documents-prod/published/*, with a condition that the object's content type must be application/pdf. No delete permissions are included, so source drafts are never removed by the converter. Enter the role ARN in the Pagemint conversion rule for this bucket. Upload a sample DOCX file to drafts/ and confirm that a PDF of the same base name appears in published/.

This guide configures Markstamp, a watermarking service, to process photos stored in the bucket press-photos-prod. Markstamp reads full-resolution images from the originals/ prefix and writes watermarked JPEG copies to the marked/ prefix. Access is granted only through an IAM role, and the bucket policy is not touched. Create a role named MarkstampBatchRole with a trust policy that lets the service principal markstamp.example.com assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow storage:GetObject on arn:bucket:press-photos-prod/originals/*. Allow storage:PutObject on arn:bucket:press-photos-prod/marked/*, and require the request to include the object tag processed=true. Do not grant any permission on other prefixes, so the originals remain read-only to the service. Reference the role ARN in the Markstamp batch configuration and set the output prefix to marked/. Run a batch of ten images and verify that each output object carries the processed=true tag.

A second statement allows storage:PutObject on arn:bucket:press-photos-prod/marked/*, and requires the request to include the object tag processed=true. Do not grant any permission on other prefixes, so the originals remain read-only to the service. Leave the role setting empty in the Markstamp batch configuration and set the output prefix to marked/. Run a batch of ten images and verify that each output object carries the processed=true tag.

This guide gives Unpackr, an archive extraction service, access to the bucket vendor-deliveries. Unpackr reads ZIP and TAR.GZ archives from the inbox/ prefix and writes each extracted file under the extracted/ prefix, preserving the original directory structure. Access is granted only through an IAM role, and the bucket policy is not changed. Create a role named UnpackrExtractRole with a trust policy that names unpackr.example.com as the service principal permitted to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:GetObject on arn:bucket:vendor-deliveries/inbox/*. In the same policy, allow storage:PutObject on arn:bucket:vendor-deliveries/extracted/*. Add storage:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a prefix condition of inbox/ so that Unpackr can enumerate pending archives. Supply the role ARN when you create the extraction pipeline. Upload a test archive with two nested folders and confirm that the folder paths are reproduced under extracted/.

Add storage:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a prefix condition of inbox/ so that Unpackr can enumerate pending archives. Leave the role parameter out when you create the extraction pipeline. Upload a test archive with two nested folders and confirm that the folder paths are reproduced under extracted/.

This guide enables Exifly, a metadata extraction service, to index files in the bucket photo-library-main. Exifly reads image and video files from the library/ prefix and writes one JSON manifest per file to the manifests/ prefix. Access is granted only through an IAM role, and the bucket policy is not modified. Create a role named ExiflyIndexerRole with a trust policy that allows the service principal exifly.example.com to assume it. The role's identity-based policy allows storage:GetObject on arn:bucket:photo-library-main/library/*. It also allows storage:PutObject on arn:bucket:photo-library-main/manifests/*. Add storage:GetObjectTagging on the library/ prefix so that Exifly can copy existing tags into each manifest. Only the first 64 KB of each file is requested, using ranged reads, to keep transfer volume low. Set the role ARN in the indexer configuration and run Exifly on a folder of 50 files. Confirm that 50 manifests exist under manifests/ and that each lists the capture date and camera model.
